Anthropic神秘模型攻克量子计算重要猜想，困扰数学界近20年的难题解决了

动察 Beating AI 快讯，AI 研究公司 Physical Superintelligence（PSI）宣布，借助 Anthropic 一款尚未发布的模型，证明了困扰数学界近 20 年的 Aaronson–Ambainis 猜想。AI 在运行第三天就找到了完整证明，并通过 Lean 数学验证工具的检查。

这项猜想由两位科学家在 2008 年提出，研究的是量子计算机的速度优势究竟有多大。

量子计算机在处理某些问题时，可能比普通计算机快上亿倍。比如分解一个特别大的整数，普通计算机用已知算法可能需要极长时间，量子计算机则有望大幅缩短计算时间。但这种巨大优势通常依赖问题本身存在某种数学规律。

这次 AI 证明，如果输入的数据完全随机，没有可利用的特殊规律，那么对于只需要回答「是」或「否」的问题，量子计算机就无法在读取数据的次数上取得指数级优势。

比如要从海量随机数字中判断一个结果，量子计算机可以利用量子叠加，一次查询涉及多个位置。普通计算机虽然每次只能读取一个位置，但只要知道量子算法的判断规则，就能优先检查那些最影响结果的数字，用相对有限的查询次数，近似预测量子计算机的答案。

此前，数学家已经知道某些特殊情况下可以做到这一点，却一直无法证明这条规律普遍成立。PSI 这次完成了完整证明，也解决了一个延续近 20 年的理论问题。

消息传出后，华盛顿大学教授 Pedro Domingos 甚至认为，量子计算优势的梦想已经破灭。

猜想提出者之一 Scott Aaronson 随后指出，这种理解是错的。研究限制的只是特定问题中量子计算机能节省多少次数据查询，并没有否定量子计算机的实际运算速度优势。用于大整数分解的 Shor 算法，以及量子物理、化学模拟，都不受影响。

Aaronson 表示，自己还没完全读懂这份证明，但 Lean 已经完成检查，也有其他数学家审阅过，因此他相信结果正确。他还开玩笑说，虽然高兴自己的猜想终于得到证明，但也有些失望，人类最终没能赶在 AI 前面解决它。

Coinbase’s US national trust bank charter takes effect
Coinbase plans to expand its institutional crypto custody business under the federal charter and is exploring digital asset payment products.
Coinbase’s national trust bank charter took effect on Friday, according to the US Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC).
The applied for the charter in October 2025 and received preliminary approval in April 2026, according to the OCC’s filing record. The charter allows Coinbase National Trust Company to hold digital assets on behalf of clients as a fiduciary, according to the OCC’s preliminary approval letter.
Coinbase plans to offer institutional clients segregated custody accounts, with access to staking, financing and trading through other Coinbase entities, according to its charter application.
Coinbase’s application also outlined plans to explore digital asset payment products and custody services that would allow clients to interact with select smart contracts.
Other crypto companies that received OCC national trust bank charters include Ripple, Circle, BitGo, Fidelity Digital Assets and Paxos.
Crypto.com and Stripe-owned Bridge received conditional approval, while Kraken and EDX Markets are still pursuing charters.

Trezor Investigation Update: Malicious Circuit Boards Found in Three Safe 5 Wallets

Hardware wallet manufacturer Trezor provided an update on its investigation into hardware tampering involving devices sold by reseller CryptoBilis. After inspecting devices from 48 users who contacted the company, Trezor confirmed that three Trezor Safe 5 wallets sold between August 20 and September 23, 2026, through CryptoBilis and its Tokopedia and Shopee stores contained malicious circuit boards. The implants, concealed between the motherboard and display, could capture recovery seeds and passphrases shown on the screen and transmit them to attackers’ servers via cellular networks. No user funds have been reported stolen to date. Trezor has reduced its reseller network by approximately 80%, tightened procurement and warehousing controls, and released firmware version 2.13.1 on November 11 to block data capture by the identified implants. Customers who purchased devices from CryptoBilis since March 2026 are eligible for a free replacement or refund. — link

--- From rss ---
Crypto wallet firm Trezor has cut its reseller network by 80% following the discovery of more spy implants in devices sold by Malaysian vendor CryptoBilis.
Trezor’s latest update on the spyware incident revealed it has implemented stricter rules for vendors in order to protect its supply chain.
However, only 20% of vendors were able to abide by the new rules that focus on “how devices are sourced, stored and who has access to them.”
Trezor stressed, however, that the dropped resellers “were trustworthy and posed no immediate threat.”
Trezor says its new update renders spy implants useless
Trezor also claims to have released an update on November 11 that stops the implants recording data and renders them “useless.”
A spokesperson for the company told Protos, “The implant listens to the communication between the MCU and the display and triggers the capture when it sees a specific sequence.”
In order to stop the sequence trigger, which is a wallet’s seed phrase, Trezor claims it “changed the order of the commands sent to the display” and that it can do this “without any effect on the displayed screen.”
Read more: Trezor reveals Malaysian reseller sold wallet with spyware
Despite this, Trezor warned CryptoBilis customers that they should still move their funds to a new wallet as “the update can’t protect a wallet backup that was captured before it.”
Three Trezor wallets infected but no funds stolen
Trezor says a total of three Trezor Safe 5 models have been found implanted with the spyware and that the devices were purchased between August 20 and September 23.
It still maintains that no crypto has been stolen from the affected devices, and has offered those who bought their wallets from CryptoBilis a free replacement.
Ledger wallet users suffered $86M theft
Wallets sold by Trezor rival Ledger were drained of over $86 million last month in an attack that also involved tampered wallets sold by CryptoBilis.
Stablecoin firm Tether froze $10 million in stolen funds, and Ledger asked multiple wallet vendors across Asia to halt sales.
Read more: Ledger roasted over $849 device launch after $86M hack
Its investigation uncovered an organized crime group spending millions to build spyware infrastructure that involved logistics, seed collector servers, and draining/laundering infrastructure.
It took several weeks before Trezor revealed it too had discovered an implant in one of its devices.

The US securities clearinghouse plans to bring tokenized stocks to Solana in 2027, but analysts say restrictions could limit adoption.
Plans by the Depository Trust & Clearing Corporation’s (DTCC) to bring tokenized securities to Solana could attract more traditional financial institutions to the blockchain, but regulatory restrictions may limit the impact on the network, according to analysts.
DTCC announced Thursday that it plans to connect its tokenization service to Solana in the second half of 2027. The move would allow certain securities held by its Depository Trust Company (DTC) subsidiary to be turned into digital tokens on the network.
Solana is a blockchain known for its fast transactions and low fees, making it popular for crypto trading, especially memecoins. The network had about $4.94 billion in total value locked (TVL) as of Nov. 12, according to DefiLlama.
Experts say the move could help Solana attract more activity beyond just memecoins, but it’s not clear how much new capital and transaction volume it could bring to the network. What’s more, current US regulatory rules still limit who can hold and transfer the tokenized assets.
Memes paved the way
Alex Lin, founding partner at venture capital firm Reforge, said Solana’s history of handling large amounts of memecoin trading may have helped show that the network can support traditional financial activity.
“Memes were a public stress test that gave Solana credibility that it can handle retail-scale volume cheaply and reliably,” Lin told Cointelegraph. “The casino paved the way for more institutional plumbing.”
However, under a December 2025 SEC no-action letter, DTC participants must register wallets to hold tokenized securities. The tokens can only be transferred between registered wallets, potentially limiting usage.
“It’s overstated in the near term because the SEC relief from Dec 2025 keeps these tokens in a walled garden of registered DTC participants, so permissionless retail and DeFi liquidity can’t touch these tokens directly yet,” Lin said. “Regulators need to let these assets work as true onchain collateral and that’s more policy than tech.”
DTCC launched its tokenization service on the Canton Network and its private Besu network on Oct. 28, allowing certain securities to be turned into digital tokens while keeping the same investor protections. At launch, DTCC said 20 DTC participants had signed agreements to access the service, but it has not said whether any plan to use Solana.
Cointelegraph contacted DTCC and the Solana Foundation for additional comments but has not yet heard back.

Solana trading slows, but tokenized assets grow
Kha Nguyen, CEO and co-founder of blockchain analytics platform Birdeye, which tracks trading activity on Solana, said the blockchain has already seen growing demand for tokenized stocks without DTCC’s involvement.
According to Birdeye’s H1 2026 report, tokenized-stock trading volume on Solana reached around $4.9 billion in the first half of the year, more than six times the volume recorded in the previous six months.
Birdeye’s third-quarter report also found that more than 1 million accounts held tokenized stocks on Solana by late September.
Still, broader trading activity on Solana has slowed with the network recording about 6.9 billion transactions in the 30 days ending Nov. 11, down almost 40% from the previous 30-day period, according to Token Terminal data. What could happen next?
Nguyen said DTCC’s integration would need support from banks and other financial firms to have a real impact on Solana. Institutions would also need enough liquidity to support large trades.
“Banks, brokers and issuers need to say they will issue, trade and settle there, and then do it,” Nguyen said. He added that institutions would need to actively use the tokenized securities rather than simply hold them.
“The assets must be active, not idle: traded around the clock, used as collateral to borrow against, and earning yield,” Nguyen said.

items.content: MSCI to drop Strategy from global indexes, putting billions in fund inflows at risk  Reuters --- From rss --- In brief - MSCI will remove Strategy’s MSTR shares from its MSCI USA Index, affecting broader global benchmarks, after November 30. - The index provider’s new rules target companies that resemble investment funds rather than operating businesses. - Selling by index-tracking funds could pressure Strategy’s stock, potentially reducing the money it can raise to buy Bitcoin. Strategy made $19.53 billion in profit last quarter. Yet MSCI, one of the world’s biggest providers of stock indexes, has decided Michael Saylor’s Bitcoin company no longer belongs in some of its major investment benchmarks. MSCI’s November review lists “STRATEGY A”—the company’s MSTR shares—for deletion from the MSCI USA Index after trading closes November 30. That also removes the stock from broader indexes that include U.S. companies, such as the MSCI World and MSCI All Country World indexes. That sounds technical, but the distinction matters: MSCI is not removing Strategy from the Nasdaq stock exchange, shutting down its business, or making it sell Bitcoin. It is taking MSTR out of stock lists that investment funds use to decide which companies to own. Will Strategy hold over 1M BTC before 2027? Consider an ETF designed to copy the MSCI USA Index. When MSTR disappears from the list, the fund generally has to sell its shares, regardless of whether the fund manager likes Saylor’s strategy. This is why it’s bad news for Strategy. It means less indirect exposition to investments. Why is MSCI kicking Strategy out? MSCI adopted new rules in October for so-called non-operating companies. The idea is to keep investment vehicles—businesses that mainly hold financial assets—out of indexes meant to track operating companies. Its screening process considers a company’s operating assets and other financial measures. MSCI’s deletion list does not spell out exactly which tests Strategy failed. The company, however, argues that raising capital, managing its Bitcoin treasury and issuing financial products amount to a genuine operating business. In an August letter to MSCI, Strategy called the proposal “discriminatory, arbitrary, and misguided.” It argued that MSCI should be a “mirror of the market, not an arbiter of it.” Strategy also maintains a software business, but Bitcoin now dominates its finances. The disagreement is whether its Bitcoin activity counts as running a company or mainly managing an investment portfolio. Strategy’s latest quarterly earnings show $19.53 billion in net income. But that does not mean its software customers paid the company anything close to that amount. Nearly all of its $20.91 billion in reported operating income came from a rise in the accounting value of its Bitcoin. Under rules adopted in 2025, changes in Bitcoin’s market price appear in Strategy’s earnings even when it has not sold the coins. A decline in Bitcoin can produce the opposite result. Its software division, meanwhile, recorded $125.4 million in quarterly revenue, down 3% from a year earlier. Its $477.2 million in revenue for all of 2025 was slightly below the $486.3 million reported in 2019, before Strategy began buying Bitcoin. Could this hurt Bitcoin? The immediate risk is selling pressure on MSTR, not on Bitcoin itself. Strategy estimated that funds linked to MSCI indexes hold roughly 13 million of its shares, or 3.1% of its outstanding common stock. Not all of that necessarily translates into sudden sales, and Strategy says the amount is manageable. But Strategy has repeatedly raised money by selling shares and other securities, then used those proceeds to buy Bitcoin. If its stock falls, selling the same number of new shares brings in less cash. So the company would have to issue more shares to raise the same amount—or buy fewer Bitcoin. That is why a stock-index decision could eventually matter to the crypto market. The exclusion does not force a Bitcoin sale, and it does not guarantee fewer purchases. It could, however, weaken a key source of funding for one of Bitcoin’s biggest corporate buyers. items.content:
In brief
- Colette Kress, 59, became Nvidia's interim CEO following Jensen Huang's resignation, while retaining her CFO responsibilities.
- She joined Nvidia in 2013 after nearly 25 years at Texas Instruments, Microsoft, and Cisco, helping oversee a more than 50-fold increase in annual revenue.
- Her biggest challenges include maintaining investor confidence, navigating US-China tensions, and managing an organization built around Huang's leadership.
For the first time in 33 years, someone other than Jensen Huang is running Nvidia. And the person taking over is not an engineer, a chip designer, or a Silicon Valley founder.
Colette Kress, Nvidia's 59-year-old chief financial officer, was named interim CEO Thursday following Huang's abrupt resignation amid reports of extramarital affairs and allegations involving a suspected Chinese intelligence operative.
Kress will remain CFO while the board searches for a permanent replacement, according to Nvidia's regulatory filing. She inherits a company worth trillions of dollars, a shaken investor base, and a management structure built around one man.
From Texas Instruments to Nvidia's AI empire
Kress joined Nvidia in September 2013, when it was primarily known for graphics cards used in video games. She arrived with nearly 25 years of financial experience across some of America's largest technology companies.
She spent eight years at Texas Instruments before joining Microsoft in 1997. During her 13-year tenure there, she became CFO of the Server and Tools division, overseeing financial strategy for Microsoft's enterprise computing business.
In 2010, she moved to Cisco as senior vice president and CFO of its Business Technology and Operations Finance organization, managing financial planning and business development across the networking giant's operations.
Kress holds a finance degree from the University of Arizona and an MBA from Southern Methodist University, according to her official biography.
Her move to Nvidia came with an unusual endorsement. Her two sons, then enthusiastic gamers, encouraged her to join the company responsible for the graphics chips powering their favorite games, according to Forbes.
Huang personally recruited her, explaining his vision for AI computing on a whiteboard during their discussions, Wired reported. At the time, Nvidia was the smallest company Kress had worked for.
The woman behind Nvidia's financial expansion
When Kress joined Nvidia, its annual revenue stood at approximately $4.13 billion. By fiscal 2026, that figure had reached $215.9 billion, an increase of more than 50 times.
Huang drove Nvidia's technological strategy, but Kress oversaw the finances supporting its expansion from gaming hardware into data centers and AI infrastructure.
Her tenure included Nvidia's $6.9 billion acquisition of networking specialist Mellanox and an increasingly aggressive strategy of investing in companies that purchase its computing hardware.
Those relationships now include CoreWeave, in which Nvidia invested another $2 billion in January. CoreWeave's rapid growth reflects enormous demand for Nvidia-powered computing, alongside the financial costs of building that infrastructure.
Kress also became Nvidia's principal financial voice to Wall Street, regularly explaining margins, chip demand and revenue forecasts during earnings calls.
Forbes ranked her among America's richest self-made women in 2026, with almost $750 million in Nvidia shares as of Wednesday's close.
The challenges
Kress takes charge as Nvidia faces questions about the sustainability of AI infrastructure spending. Nvidia had already lost approximately $1.27 trillion in market value from its October peak before the board publicly announced its investigation on Huang’s love affairs.
She must also navigate Washington's restrictions on advanced chip exports to China and scrutiny surrounding Nvidia's commercial relationships. The board has said it has no reason to believe company secrets or U.S. national security were compromised in the allegations involving Huang.
Her financial expertise cannot entirely replace Huang's technical background or his personal relationships with developers, customers, and governments. Maintaining Nvidia's engineering leadership will require close coordination with the executives responsible for its chips and software.
Kress has promised to build on Huang's legacy, saying that “Nvidia's strength has always come from its people.”
Her first major public test arrives Tuesday, November 17, when Nvidia reports its third-quarter fiscal 2027 earnings. The company has scheduled its results for approximately 1:20 p.m. Pacific, followed by an investor call at 2 p.m.

North Korean hackers create memecoins to launder funds
North Korean hackers created memecoins to launder cryptocurrency stolen in the $6.3 billion Binance hack, according to a report from blockchain analytics firm Elliptic.
Between Nov. 5 and 7, the hackers created at least six tokens on NEAR and used liquidity pools on decentralized exchanges to move $430,000 of stolen funds between wallets, Elliptic said. However, the tokens attracted almost no outside trading and were abandoned shortly after launch.
Elliptic said the same laundering technique was also used following the $1.5 billion Bybit hack in 2025, when North Korean-linked actors moved at least $24 million through a newly created token on the TRON blockchain.

Payward said it plans to add hundreds of Hong Kong-listed equities in the coming weeks.
Hong Kong’s forthcoming crypto licensing regime
Deputy Secretary for Financial Services Chan Ho-lim told FinTech Week the region will introduces a new licensing regime for virtual-asset trading, custody, advisory and management, via amendment bills that will be submitted to Legislative Council this year.

South Korea’s Financial Services Commission (FSC) plans to allow crypto exchanges to suspend deposits and withdrawals when hacking is suspected, rather than waiting until a breach is confirmed.
The FSC said it would issue a no-action letter permitting preventive suspensions under certain conditions. Current rules prohibit exchanges from blocking withdrawals without legitimate grounds and explicitly allow restrictions only when a hacking incident is clearly established.
The regulator also called for round-the-clock monitoring and incident response, higher cold-wallet holdings, and stronger insurance coverage and reserves.

Coinbase CEO：即将推出Coinbase Pro，正推进AI金融账户与美国股票永续合约

BlockBeats 消息，11 月 13 日，Coinbase 首席执行官 Brian Armstrong 发文表示，Coinbase 将其托管的逾 99% 加密资产存放在冷钱包，并使用最新 AI 模型加强防御，有时会提前获得模型访问权限。他表示，Coinbase 的安全设计考虑到员工可能受骗，任何单个人、单台电脑或单一系统都无法独立转移用户资金。他还称，全球规模最大的银行中有 7 家选择与 Coinbase 合作，Coinbase 在全球持有 80 多项牌照。

AI 智能体金融是 Coinbase 的重点方向。Armstrong 援引预测称，到 2030 年，AI 智能体处理的交易规模可能达到 3 万亿至 5 万亿美元。他认为，加密网络适合作为智能体执行交易的基础设施，开发面向 AI 智能体的金融账户是 Coinbase 的优先事项之一。

股票代币化方面，Armstrong 称，Base 上的代币化股票交易量已超过 50 亿美元。他认为，代币化股票比传统股票更易获取，还可与 DeFi 协议结合，例如让持有人利用股票资产获取收益。

美国股票永续合约方面，Armstrong 表示，Coinbase 多年来一直推动这类产品在美国合规落地，并对 SEC 与 CFTC 负责人就此开展合作表示欢迎。他指出，股票永续合约已在美国境外市场交易。他还预告 Coinbase Pro 即将推出，但未在帖文中给出具体时间。

美国现货比特币ETF连续两周净流出23.5亿美元，贝莱德IBIT遭遇连续11个交易日资金撤出

BlockBeats 消息，11 月 14 日，美国现货比特币 ETF 已连续两周净流出，累计规模达 23.5 亿美元。其中，11 月 9 日至 13 日净流出 10.7 亿美元，此前一周净流出 12.8 亿美元。

周五，美国现货比特币 ETF 单日净流出 1.854 亿美元，其中贝莱德 IBIT 净流出 1.435 亿美元，富达 FBTC 净流出 4,190 万美元。这也是美国现货比特币 ETF 连续第七个交易日出现资金净流出，自 11 月 5 日以来累计净流出约 17.1 亿美元。

其中，贝莱德 IBIT 已连续 11 个交易日遭遇资金净流出，累计流出约 23.5 亿美元。该基金 11 月以来净流出达 21.2 亿美元，约占同期美国现货比特币 ETF 总净流出规模的 90%。

Bitcoin ETFs shed $2.35B in two weeks as BlackRock’s losing streak hits 11 sessions
US spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded $185.4 million in net outflows Friday, with BlackRock’s IBIT accounting for $143.5 million and Fidelity’s FBTC shedding $41.9 million.
US spot Bitcoin exchange-traded funds (ETFs) recorded $2.35 billion in net outflows over two consecutive weeks, as redemptions reached more than $1 billion each week.
According to Farside Investors data, spot Bitcoin ETFs shed $1.07 billion between Nov. 9 and Nov. 13, following $1.28 billion in outflows the previous week, the largest weekly redemptions since late June.
The funds recorded $185.4 million in net outflows on Friday, down from $284.1 million on Thursday and $299.8 million on Wednesday. BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT) accounted for $143.5 million of Friday’s withdrawals, while Fidelity’s Wise Origin Bitcoin Fund (FBTC) shed $41.9 million.
Friday marked the seventh consecutive trading session of net withdrawals, with about $1.71 billion redeemed since Nov. 5. The sustained outflows coincided with broader market weakness as Bitcoin (BTC) fell below $70,000 on the same day.
BlackRock’s Bitcoin ETF extends losing streak to 11 sessions
IBIT’s $143.5 million in net outflows on Friday extended the fund’s withdrawal streak to 11 consecutive trading sessions since Oct. 30.
The latest losses brought IBIT’s total net outflows over the 11-session streak to about $2.35 billion, extending withdrawals after outflows crossed the $2 billion mark on Wednesday.
IBIT shed $908.4 million during the latest week, following approximately $1.21 billion in withdrawals the previous week. Its November outflows reached $2.12 billion, accounting for roughly 90% of the broader Bitcoin ETF market’s net withdrawals during the month.

【Web3Auth 发布安全事件更新，服务将逐步恢复】

Foresight News 消息，Web3Auth 发布安全事件更新。11 月 7 日，其基础设施出现安全问题，影响使用 Google 或 Apple 登录创建的部分嵌入式钱包（包括 Torus Wallet 及 Keplr 等第三方应用所用钱包），导致部分账户被未授权访问。自 11 月 8 日起，Web3Auth 已启动白帽资产回收操作，将风险资产转移至安全回收钱包，并公布多链验证地址。现有用户登录功能已逐步恢复，但需升级至 SDK v10 或 v11。新用户注册预计于 11 月 23 日前在迁移后的 Legacy 网络重新开放。

Polkadot Plans dotUSD, a DOT-Backed Stablecoin Pegged to the U.S. Dollar

The Polkadot Community Foundation (PCF) said its proposed strategy passed an onchain governance referendum on November 11 with 97% support. Polkadot will shift its focus from building infrastructure to developing products for everyday users, including a mobile app for private messaging and digital cash payments.

The platform will center on dotStables, starting with dotUSD, a U.S. dollar-pegged stablecoin backed by DOT and designed to drive demand for DOT as adoption grows. Polkadot will use user adoption and product usage as key measures of progress and direct more marketing funds toward campaigns tied to measurable user engagement. — link
